item.title: Two scientists want to touch Saturn's rings: NASA says this daring mission could actually work
item.description: For centuries, space has fascinated humans like no other. From the sun's glare to the moon's surface and even Saturn's shimmering rings, we have wanted to go up close and see it all. Now, two ambitious NASA-backed projects aim to truly touch Saturn's rings, venturing into what is known as one of the most dangerous environments in the solar system.

item.title: In 1937, a botanical garden in Tahiti planted an ornamental tree; today, a single tree can produce 8.9 million seeds and threaten Queensland’s World Heritage rainforests
item.description: An ornamental tree planted in Tahiti in 1937 now poses a serious biosecurity threat. This invasive miconia species aggressively invades forests and smothers native vegetation. A single mature tree can produce millions of seeds, rapidly spreading across landscapes. Queensland's World Heritage rainforests face irreversible ecological damage from this plant. Early detection and eradication efforts are crucial to protect these precious ecosystems.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Scientists warn melting glaciers could form more than 50,000 new lakes in areas covered by ice
item.description: In a study published in Nature Communications, researchers from Sweden, US, Switzerland and Norway mapped what lies beneath all the glaciers on the planet and reached a shocking conclusion: when part of this ice disappears, Earth could gain 56,659 new lakes in areas currently completely frozen. This could increase the risk of flooding in Asia, Andes, Alaska and the Arctic
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Canva's billionaire founders donated $150 million directly to residents of Malawi; aided 90% rise above extreme poverty
item.description: Canva billionaires Melanie Perkins and Cliff Obrecht have made a move challenging conventional aid by putting cash directly into the hands of an East African country's poorest households. The cofounders of the Australian design software maker are investing a whopping $150 million into a cash transfer program in Malawi. Since launching the initiative in 2021 through the Canva Foundation and nonprofit GiveDirectly, the couple has expanded what began as a $10 million pilot into the largest unconditional cash transfer program ever attempted in a low-income country.

item.description: Ukraine's Emergency Services said rescue operations at the site, located north of the capital, had been completed. item.title: SK Group chairman Chey Tae-won ordered to pay ex-wife Roh Soh-yeong $644M in divorce settlement
item.description: A South Korean appeals court on Friday ordered SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won to pay his former wife, Roh Soh-yeong, 944 billion won (about $644 million) in cash as part of their long-running divorce property settlement, while reaffirming that Chey's SK shares formed part of the couple's marital assets.

item.title: Donald Trump returns to White House Correspondents' dinner months after shooting forced postponement
item.description: President Trump attended the rescheduled White House Correspondents' Association dinner. This event followed a shooting incident outside the original venue in April. The president addressed journalists from major news organizations after months of media clashes. The dinner celebrated press freedom and raised money for journalism scholarships. Heightened security measures were in place for Friday's event at the Waldorf Astoria.

item.title: Quote of the day by Michael Faraday: 'There's nothing quite as frightening as someone who knows...'
item.description: The danger of absolute certainty lies in its ability to stifle necessary discussions and overlook crucial warning signs. Renowned scientist Michael Faraday emphasized the importance of maintaining doubt and curiosity in our thoughts. Psychological studies reveal that a limited understanding can cause individuals to mistakenly inflate their competence. In leadership, rigid mindsets can have disastrous consequences throughout history. Embracing new information and perspectives is essential for our survival.

item.title: YouTuber Joe Is Hungry says he never expected his KFC Popcorn Chicken review to go viral
item.description: Food reviewer Joe Is Hungry expressed surprise at his KFC Popcorn Chicken video's popularity. The video garnered nearly twenty million views across various social media platforms. Joe admitted he did not anticipate such widespread attention for the review. He also discussed the challenges involved in creating his unique food review videos. His distinctive filming style and honest reactions continue to attract a large audience.
